sources.name: Small Wind Site Assessment Guidelines
sources.verificationNote: Read in full on 2026-09-25 from the laboratory's document server (docs.nlr.gov; the nrel.gov host no longer resolves): section 5.3.2 prints the power law V = Vref × (h / href)^α, and Table 1 (Textbook Versus Measured Wind Shear by Terrain Type) gives the textbook exponents used: calm sea 0.09, cut grass 0.14, crops and tall-grass prairie 0.19, scattered trees and hedges 0.24, city suburbs, villages, and scattered forests 0.31, woodlands 0.43. The report has no worked numeric example of the power law.

sources.name: Wind Resource Assessment Handbook
sources.verificationNote: Read on 2026-09-25 from docs.nlr.gov: section 3.1, page 3-3, gives the power law v2 = v1 × (z2 / z1)^α and says α is often taken as 0.143, the 1/7th power law, for a well-mixed atmosphere over flat, open terrain, with higher values over vegetation and in light winds; page 9-6 solves the law for α. No worked numeric example.

sources.name: Pix4D ground control point guidance
sources.verificationNote: Checked at the issuer on 2026-09-25: the PIX4Dmapper page "Getting GCPs on the field or through other sources" (undated) asks for at least 3 GCPs, recommends at least 5, says 5 to 10 are usually enough even for large projects, and advises placing them evenly, one in the center, and not exactly at the edges of the area.
